title: Common Exception Words (KS1)
subject: English
strapline: The tricky words that don't play by the phonics rules — learn them by sight.
facts: Common exception words are words you can't fully sound out with the phonics rules you know yet, so you learn them by sight.
Year 1 examples: the, a, do, to, today, of, said, says, are, were, was, is, his, has, I, you, your.
More Year 1 words: they, be, he, me, she, we, no, go, so, by, my, here, there, love, come, some.
Year 2 examples: door, floor, poor, because, find, kind, mind, behind, child, wild, climb, most, only.
More Year 2 words: both, old, cold, gold, hold, told, every, great, break, steak, pretty, beautiful, after, fast, last, past.
The odd part is usually just one or two letters — "said" is s-ai-d but "ai" makes an /e/ sound here.
Practise reading them fast on flashcards, then find them in a book you are reading.

quick_quiz.q: Spell the word that means "not any": n_
Which word is the odd one out for phonics: cat, said, mat?
Finish it: "It is very ___iful" (lovely to look at).

teacher_tips: Teach them in small sets and revisit daily — little and often beats one long session.
Point out the one tricky grapheme rather than calling the whole word "irregular".
Send home a personal pack of the ones a child still finds hard, not the whole list.
